result.title: Ultrasound Elastography: Excitation Methods and Low-Cost Alternative
result.summary: Ultrasound elastography (or elasticity imaging) is a method that characterizes the tissue mechanical properties with the purpose of aiding the diagnosis of certain pathologies. Many novel clinical applications use the assumption that these tissue properties are changed in the presence of pathological processes. Characterization of tissue mechanical properties is achieved by imaging the response of the tissue to an induced stress or excitation. A plethora of approaches have been used in the scientific community to induce excitation in tissue, which usually require additional tools or devices than are costly. Furthermore these are usually integrated in the imaging pipeline using additional software or hardware for control. An alternative that is simpler, faster to integrate (and low-cost) is proposed in this work, by using readily available smartphones as a source of mechanical excitation. The induced displacements are used to solve the elasticity inverse problem (IP) using a finite element method (FEM) approach. Preliminary elasticity reconstructions of a phantom that mimics tissue are similar to when using a dedicated actuator as means of inducing harmonic displacements, illustrating the feasibility of our low-cost ultrasound elasography approach.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作提出用现成智能手机作为超声弹性成像的机械激励源，并以有限元方法求解弹性逆问题，在仿组织体模上验证了与专用激励器相近的重建效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 内容属于医学超声成像的激励装置与逆问题重建，与视觉语言模型中的 latent 表示、推理状态生成或证据筛选无实质联系，也未提供可核查的方法借鉴线索。
